Assert that rows pointing to other rows find them, and agree

Source: R/groups.R
ensure_references.Rd

A checkpoint for a column that points to another row of the same table: a spouse's cpr, a mother's cpr, the reference person of a family. Each reference must find its row, must not point to its own row, and with mutual = TRUE the row it finds must point back, as spouses do. With same, the row it finds must agree on those columns, such as the family a spouse belongs to. The rows that break a rule are reported, with a problem column saying which. Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

ensure_references(
  data,
  id,
  ref,
  within = NULL,
  same = NULL,
  mutual = FALSE,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database and Arrow tables in checkpoints.

id

The column identifying each row (one column), e.g. cpr.

ref

The column pointing to another row's id (one column), e.g. spouse.

within

Columns the row pointed to must share to be found (tidy-select), e.g. year, or NULL (default).

same

Columns the row pointed to must agree on once found (tidy-select), e.g. family, or NULL (default).

mutual

If TRUE, the row pointed to must point back. Default FALSE.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when a reference breaks a rule and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the check.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

In a panel a person has a row per year, and a reference should find the row of the same year: give the period in within, and the row is looked up among the rows with the same values there. id must be unique within within; check it with ensure_unique() first. A missing reference is no reference, and passes.

Rules about the row a reference finds, such as a mother older than her child, are written by joining its columns on and stating the rule with ensure_none():

persons |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(persons, mother = cpr, mother_born = born),
                   by = "mother") |>
  ensure_none(mother_born >= born)

See also

ensure_matched() for references to another table, ensure_counts(), checkpoints.

Examples

persons <- data.frame(
  cpr    = c("a", "b", "c", "d", "e"),
  spouse = c("b", "a", "d", "e", "x"),
  family = c(1, 1, 2, 3, 3)
)
# c points to d, who points to e; e points to x, who is not there; c and
# d are in different families
ensure_references(persons, cpr, spouse, same = family, mutual = TRUE)
#> Warning: Broken references: spouse to cpr
#> ℹ 3 rows in 3 groups
#>   Problems: does not point back (1), in another family (1), not found (1)
#> ℹ The rows:
#>     problem             cpr   spouse family
#>     <chr>               <chr> <chr>   <dbl>
#>   1 in another family   c     d           2
#>   2 does not point back d     e           3
#>   3 not found           e     x           3
